quote: business_logic: '- Group campaign-level rows by platform, account_id normalized by replacing NULL with ''0'' and casting to text, and date_day. - Set segmentation fields not used at account level to NULL: ad_network_type, device, interaction_event_types. - Aggregate totals across all campaigns in each group: - Sum impressions, clicks, interactions, cost, conversions, conversions_value, and view_through_conversions; missing values are ignored, and if all values are missing the result is NULL. - For active view sums (impressions, measurable impressions, measurable cost), treat missing row values as 0 before summing; if all inputs are missing the result is 0. - For active view averages (measurability, viewability), treat missing row values as 0 and take the unweighted average across rows. - Derived metrics (computed from the aggregated totals): - Click-through rate (percent) = total clicks / total impressions × 100, rounded to 4 decimals; returns 0 if total impressions is not greater than 0; returns NULL if total clicks is NULL while impressions are positive. - Cost per click = total cost / total clicks, rounded to 2 decimals; returns 0 if total clicks is not greater than 0; returns NULL if total cost is NULL while clicks are positive. - Cost per thousand impressions = total cost / total impressions × 1000, rounded to 2 decimals; returns 0 if total impressions is not greater than 0; returns NULL if total cost is NULL while impressions are positive. - Cost per conversion = total cost / total conversions, rounded to 2 decimals; returns 0 if total conversions is not greater than 0; returns NULL if total cost is NULL while conversions are positive. - Return on ad spend = total conversion value / total cost, rounded to 4 decimals; returns 0 unless both totals are greater than 0. - _dbt_loaded_at is the latest timestamp across grouped rows (MAX); if all inputs are missing, the result is NULL.'

    CAST("account_id" AS VARCHAR) AS "account_id",
    CAST("date_day" AS DATE) AS "date_day",
    CAST("ad_network_type" AS INTEGER) AS "ad_network_type",

business_logic: '- Build customer_touchpoints by unifying: - Google Ads: platform=''google_ads''; use account_id as both customer_id and account_id; include campaign_id, date_day, impressions, clicks, spend as cost, conversions, conversions_value; keep only rows with account_id present. - Amazon Ads: platform=''amazon_ads''; no customer_id or account_id; include campaign_id, date_day, impressions, clicks, cost, purchases_30_d as conversions, sales_30_d as revenue_30d. - Facebook Ads: platform=''facebook_ads''; no customer_id; use account_id; set campaign_id from ad_id (as text), date_day from date; include impressions, inline_link_clicks as clicks, spend as cost; set conversions to 0. - For each touchpoint: - customer_identifier uses customer_id when available; otherwise account_id as text; otherwise the string ''UNKNOWN_'' followed by campaign_id. - revenue per touchpoint uses conversions_value when present; otherwise revenue_30d; otherwise 0. - interaction_type is ''CONVERTING_CLICK'' when both clicks and conversions are positive; ''NON_CONVERTING_CLICK'' when clicks are positive only; ''IMPRESSION_ONLY'' when impressions are positive only; otherwise ''OTHER''. - Aggregate per customer_identifier into customer_segments: - active_days is the count of unique interaction dates; platforms_used is the count of unique platforms; campaigns_interacted is the count of unique campaigns. - total_impressions, total_clicks, total_cost, total_conversions, and total_revenue are sums over touchpoints (adding only non-null values). - first_interaction_date is the earliest interaction date; last_interaction_date is the latest; customer_lifespan_days is the number of days between them. - click_to_conversion_rate is conversions divided by clicks, scaled by 100 and rounded to 2 decimals; returns 0 when clicks are missing or not positive. - impression_to_click_rate is clicks divided by impressions, scaled by 100 and rounded to 4 decimals; returns 0 when impressions are missing or not positive. - average_order_value is revenue divided by conversions, rounded to 2 decimals; returns 0 when conversions are missing or not positive. - customer_roas is revenue divided by cost, rounded to 4 decimals; returns 0 when cost is missing or not positive. - Final output per customer_identifier: - acquisition_cohort is the month of first_interaction_date; days_since_acquisition is the days from first_interaction_date to today. - customer_value_tier by total_revenue: >=1000 HIGH_VALUE; >=500 MEDIUM_VALUE; >=100 LOW_VALUE; >0 MINIMAL_VALUE; else NO_VALUE. - engagement_level: if active_days>=10 and platforms_used>=2 then HIGHLY_ENGAGED; else if active_days>=5 or platforms_used>=2 then MODERATELY_ENGAGED; else if active_days>=2 then LIGHTLY_ENGAGED; else SINGLE_INTERACTION. - conversion_behavior by total_conversions: >=5 FREQUENT_CONVERTER; >=2 REPEAT_CONVERTER; =1 SINGLE_CONVERTER; else NON_CONVERTER. - recency_status by days since last_interaction_date: <=7 RECENT; <=30 MODERATE; <=90 DORMANT; else INACTIVE. - total_cost_attributed equals total_cost; all attribution revenue fields equal total_revenue. - Cohort placeholders: cohort_size=100; retained_month_1=85; retained_month_2=72; retained_month_3=63; retention_rate_month_1=85.0; retention_rate_month_2=72.0; retention_rate_month_3=63.0. - analysis_generated_at is the run timestamp with timezone. - Filter: keep customers with first_interaction_date in the last 12 months; order by total_revenue descending, then customer_identifier ascending. - Determinism and null policy: - Per-touchpoint revenue is never null due to fallback; sums add non-null values and yield null only if all inputs are null. - Percentage rates are on a 0–100 scale, rounded as stated, and default to 0 when the denominator is missing or not positive. - Distinct counts exclude nulls and do not count duplicates.'

business_logic: 'Standardize and union campaign-day data from three ad platforms: - google_ads: use account_id as account_identifier; include campaign_id, date_day, clicks, impressions, spend as cost, conversions, and conversions_value as revenue; set platform=''google_ads'', country_code=''UNITED_STATES'', region=''NORTH_AMERICA'', local_currency=''USD''. - amazon_ads: set account_identifier to a constant (''AMZ_ACCOUNT''); include campaign_id, date_day, clicks, impressions, cost, purchases_30_d as conversions, and sales_30_d as revenue; set platform=''amazon_ads'', country_code=''UNITED_STATES'', region=''NORTH_AMERICA''; keep the reported budget currency as local_currency. - linkedin_ads: use campaign_id as account_identifier; include campaign_id, day (as a date), clicks, impressions (cast to integer), cost_in_usd (cast to numeric) as cost; derive conversions from conversion_value_in_local_currency (cast to integer, missing as 0); set revenue to 0; set platform=''linkedin_ads'', country_code=''UNITED_STATES'', region=''NORTH_AMERICA'', local_currency=''USD''; include only rows where cost_in_usd is non-negative. Aggregate the last 12 months by country_code, region, platform, and calendar month of date_day: - Market participants and volume: distinct advertisers (active_advertisers), distinct campaigns (active_campaigns), total impressions, clicks, spend, conversions, and revenue; count distinct active days (active_days_in_month). - Penetration: campaigns_per_advertiser is distinct campaigns divided by distinct advertisers (as a floating number). - KPIs with rounding and zero handling: CTR as percentage with four decimals, set to 0 when impressions are 0; CPC with two decimals, set to 0 when clicks are 0; CPM (per 1,000 impressions) with two decimals, set to 0 when impressions are 0; CPA with two decimals, set to 0 when conversions are 0; ROAS with four decimals, set to 0 unless both spend and revenue are positive. - Competitive intensity: variance and standard deviation of per-row CPC within the month; rows with zero clicks are excluded; results can be NULL if no valid values exist. Final filtering and enrichments: - Keep only months within the last six months where total_spend and total_impressions are both greater than zero. - Rename platform to marketing_channel. - Opportunity tier: HIGH_OPPORTUNITY when ROAS ≥ 3.0 and CTR ≥ 2.0; MEDIUM_OPPORTUNITY when ROAS ≥ 2.0 or CTR ≥ 1.0; OPTIMIZATION_NEEDED when ROAS < 1.0 and CTR < 0.5; otherwise MONITOR. - Growth: prev_month_spend is the previous month’s total_spend within the same country and channel after filtering; month_over_month_spend_growth is the percent change versus the previous month, rounded to two decimals, set to 0 when the previous month’s spend is not positive; the value can be negative. - Maturity tier: MATURE when active_advertisers ≥ 50 and campaigns_per_advertiser ≥ 3; DEVELOPING when active_advertisers ≥ 20 and campaigns_per_advertiser ≥ 2; EMERGING when active_advertisers ≥ 10; otherwise NASCENT. - Percentiles: spend_share_percentile is the relative position (0–1) within region and month by total_spend; performance_percentile is the relative position (0–1) within region and month by CTR. - Multi-channel metrics: avg_daily_platform_diversity is set to 1; multi_channel_advertisers equals active_advertisers; single_channel_advertisers is 0. - Analysis metadata: analysis_generated_at is the timestamp at query runtime. - Final ordering: rows are sorted by region, country_code, marketing_channel, and performance_month descending.'

business_logic: '- Source: intermediate.int_ad_reporting__campaign_report; include only rows where date_day is not null. - Derive geography per row: - region by platform: google_ads/facebook_ads/amazon_ads/linkedin_ads/microsoft_ads/pinterest_ads/snapchat_ads/reddit_ads/apple_search_ads → North America; tiktok_ads/twitter_ads → Global; else Unknown. - country_code by platform: google_ads/facebook_ads/amazon_ads → US; else Unknown. - Group by keys: platform, region, account_id, campaign_id, campaign_name, and time fields where: - month_year is the first day of the month for date_day; year is the calendar year; month is the calendar month number (1–12). - Geographic aggregates: - countries_in_region counts distinct country_code values. - country_list concatenates distinct country_code values separated by ", ", ordered ascending, excluding nulls, preserving original casing. - Aggregate metrics: - Sum impressions, clicks, interactions, cost, conversions, conversions_value, and view_through_conversions (nulls ignored). - For active_view_impressions, active_view_measurable_impressions, attributed_sales_14_d, attributed_sales_30_d, attributed_conversions_14_d, attributed_conversions_30_d: treat nulls as 0 before summing. - Derived monthly regional KPIs (division-by-zero handling and rounding): - Click-through rate: 100 times clicks divided by impressions over the group, rounded to 4 decimals; 0 when impressions are 0. - Cost per click: cost divided by clicks, rounded to 2 decimals; 0 when clicks are 0. - Cost per thousand impressions: cost per 1,000 impressions, rounded to 2 decimals; 0 when impressions are 0. - Cost per conversion: cost divided by conversions, rounded to 2 decimals; business_logic: '- Ingest four ad sources, align fields, and union: - google_ads: cost comes from spend; conversions and conversion value as provided. - amazon_ads: conversions come from purchases_30_d; revenue uses sales_30_d; no conversion value. - facebook_ads: date is converted to date_day; ad_id is treated as the campaign identifier; conversions set to 0; clicks use inline_link_clicks; cost from spend. - linkedin_ads: day is converted to date_day; ensure impressions and cost are numeric; conversions use conversion_value_in_local_currency as an integer count; exclude rows with negative cost_in_usd. - Keep only records with date_day in the last 18 months, then aggregate by date_day and platform: - Sums: impressions, clicks, cost (spend), conversions, revenue (conversion value when present, else 30‑day revenue; missing treated as 0). - KPIs: CTR = 100×(clicks/impressions) rounded to 4 decimals when impressions>0, else 0; CPC = spend/clicks rounded to 2 decimals when clicks>0, else 0; CPA = spend/conversions rounded to 2 decimals when conversions>0, else 0; ROAS = revenue/spend rounded to 4 decimals when both >0, else 0. - Campaign indicators: active_campaigns = distinct campaigns; campaigns_with_clicks = distinct campaigns with clicks>0; market_active_day = 1 when total impressions>0, else 0. - Derive calendar features: day_of_week (0=Sun..6=Sat), week_of_year, month_of_year, quarter_of_year, day_type (WEEKEND when Sun/Sat else WEEKDAY), month_period (EARLY/MID/LATE/END by day of month), and seasonal_period using explicit US seasonal date rules. For trend math, compute days since 1970‑01‑01 as a whole‑day index. - Rolling metrics are computed per platform ordered by date_day and include the current day; if fewer than N days exist, use the available days: - Moving averages: last 7 days (spend, ctr, cpc), last 30 days (spend, ctr, cpc), and last 90 days (spend). - spend_ewma is approximated as the same 7‑day simple average of spend. - Volatility: sample standard deviation over the last 30 days for ctr and cpc. - Trend and seasonality: - 90‑day rolling linear trend slopes for spend and ctr using the day index (days since epoch). - Prior‑period references: values from 365, 30, and 7 days earlier for YoY, MoM, and WoW comparisons. - Baselines: average ctr and spend by day_of_week, and by month_of_year, over the available 18‑month input window. - Anomalies and momentum: - Percent change vs prior periods is computed when the prior value is >0; otherwise NULL. - z‑scores are absolute deviations from the 30‑day mean scaled by the 30‑day standard deviation; 0 when the standard deviation is not positive. - Day‑of‑week deviation is the absolute percent difference from the day‑of‑week average; NULL when the baseline is zero. - Momentum: spend is ACCELERATING when the 7‑day average exceeds 110% of the 30‑day average, DECELERATING when below 90%, else STABLE; ctr is IMPROVING when the 7‑day average exceeds 105% of the 30‑day average, DECLINING when below 95%, else STABLE. - Trend direction from the 90‑day spend slope: STRONG_UPTREND (>0.1), MILD_UPTREND (>0 to 0.1], STRONG_DOWNTREND (<-0.1), MILD_DOWNTREND (<0 to -0.1], else SIDEWAYS. - Forecasting and confidence: - 30‑day trend forecasts add 30 times the 90‑day slope to the 30‑day average (for spend and ctr). - Seasonal factors are ratios of the daily values to the corresponding monthly averages; NULL when the monthly average is zero. - Confidence bounds are the 30‑day average minus/plus two 30‑day standard deviations. - Market signals and actions: - market_state precedence: ANOMALOUS when ctr_z_score>2 or cpc_z_score>2; else VOLATILE when WoW spend change is >50% or <‑50%; else OPTIMIZING when ctr momentum is IMPROVING and spend momentum is STABLE; else SCALING when spend momentum is ACCELERATING and ctr momentum is STABLE; else NORMAL. - requires_investigation is true when ctr_z_score>3, or cpc_z_score>3, or absolute WoW spend change exceeds 200%; otherwise false. - optimization_recommendation: OPTIMIZE_TARGETING when ctr is DECLINING and spend is ACCELERATING; OPTIMIZE_BIDDING when cpc_z_score>2 and ctr momentum is STABLE; SEASONAL_ADJUSTMENT_NEEDED when spend seasonal factor>1.2 and ctr seasonal factor<0.8; SCALE_OPPORTUNITY when market_state is SCALING; otherwise MONITOR. - Finalize by keeping only the last 12 months, ordering by platform ascending and date_day descending, and stamping analysis_generated_at with the current timestamp.'

business_logic: '- Executive KPIs (last 12 months): For each platform and month, compute monthly investment (sum of spend), average daily spend, active days, totals for impressions/clicks/conversions/revenue, average CTR/CPC/CPA/ROAS (CTR and ROAS rounded to 4 decimals; CPC and CPA to 2), and volatility as the standard deviation of daily CTR (rounded to 4) and CPC (rounded to 2). Growth and anomaly placeholders are set to zero. - Customer insights (last 12 months): For each acquisition cohort month, compute new customers (distinct count), cohort revenue (sum), average customer value and lifespan, counts of high-value, highly engaged, and frequent converters, average retention for months 1–3, average customer ROAS and order value, average platforms used per customer, and count of multi-platform customers (used more than one platform). - Geographic performance (last 6 months): For each month and region, compute active countries (distinct count), regional investment (sum), average market CTR and CPC, spend in high-opportunity markets (sum) and count of such markets, mature market ratio (share of markets classified as mature), average market share and performance percentiles, and average multi-channel adoption. - Unified performance (last 12 months): For each month, compute active platforms (distinct count), monthly totals for impressions/clicks/spend/conversions/revenue, blended averages for CTR/CPC/ROAS (rounded as above), variance across platforms for CTR (rounded to 4) and CPC (rounded to 2), designate platform leaders (CTR leader is google_ads; efficiency and ROAS leaders are amazon_ads), and campaign metrics (distinct active campaigns, average campaign age, counts of new vs established campaigns). - Strategic insights by month: - Investment efficiency grade from overall ROAS thresholds (≥3.0, ≥2.0, ≥1.0, else). - Month-over-month growth rate as percent change in monthly spend versus the prior month, rounded to 2, and set to NULL if no prior month exists. - Portfolio diversification based on active platforms and CTR variance. - Expansion mode based on the ratio of new to established campaigns. - Performance consistency based on CTR and CPC variance thresholds. - Carry forward monthly totals, blended metrics, counts, and platform leaders. - Final output: Start from strategic insights; left join platform-level KPIs by month; left join cohort-level customer insights by cohort month; left join regional geographic performance by month; filter to the last 6 reporting months; group by month and the exposed categorical fields. - Aggregate per reporting_month: customer and geographic metrics are averaged or summed across joined rows; leader platform KPIs are taken from the platform that matches the designated leader; anomaly days use the maximum; performance volatility uses the average; platform growth uses the average; scaling and optimizing days use sums. - Recommendations and strategies: - Executive recommendation based on efficiency grade, consistency, expansion status, growth rate, and overall ROAS (with a default fallback). - Allocation strategy prioritizes when efficiency and ROAS leaders align; else considers low overall ROAS; else considers high average spend in high-opportunity markets; else defaults. Comparisons against aggregated values treat NULLs as not satisfying thresholds. - Customer strategy insight evaluates retention, high-value customer mix (with zero-division protection), and cross-platform engagement, with a default fallback. - Data quality and metadata: platforms_with_data is the count of platforms present in the platform KPI join for the month (0 when none); analysis_period_start and analysis_period_end both equal the reporting_month; dashboard_generated_at is the current timestamp; results are ordered by reporting_month descending.'

business_logic: '- Build the baseline from unified campaign metrics limited to the last 12 months. - Group by platform and the calendar month of date_day; compute monthly totals (spend, impressions, clicks, conversions, 30-day revenue) and monthly averages (CTR rounded to 4 decimals, CPC rounded to 2, ROAS rounded to 4); all aggregations ignore NULLs. - Count distinct campaigns: active (all), new (lifecycle LAUNCH), and established (lifecycle ESTABLISHED); NULL campaign IDs are excluded. - Compute volatility as the standard deviation of CTR and CPC within each platform-month; if fewer than two non-NULL observations, volatility is NULL. - Per platform, order months chronologically to derive: - Month-over-month spend growth: percent change from the prior month (rounded to 2 decimals); if the prior value is not positive, set to 0. - Month-over-month CTR change: percent change from the prior month (rounded to 2 decimals); if the prior value is not positive, set to 0. - 3-month rolling averages for spend, CTR, and ROAS using the current month and two preceding months. - Spend momentum: ACCELERATING if current spend is >10% above prior month, DECELERATING if >10% below, otherwise STABLE; if no prior month, STABLE. - CTR momentum: IMPROVING if current CTR is >5% above prior month, DECLINING if >5% below, otherwise STABLE; if no prior month, STABLE. - Predictions: - Next-month spend: 3-month spend average scaled by 1.15 when accelerating, 0.85 when decelerating, otherwise unchanged. - Next-month CTR: 3-month CTR average scaled by 1.10 when improving, 0.90 when declining, otherwise unchanged. - Risk level: HIGH_RISK when CTR volatility > 0.5 and MoM spend growth > 50%; MEDIUM_RISK when CTR volatility > 0.3 or absolute MoM spend growth > 25%; otherwise LOW_RISK. - Anomaly probability: 35 when CTR volatility > 1.0 or CPC volatility > 2.0; 20 when CTR volatility > 0.5 or CPC volatility > 1.0; 25 when absolute MoM spend growth > 50%; otherwise 10. - Confidence: HIGH_CONFIDENCE when absolute MoM spend growth < 10% and CTR volatility < 0.3; MEDIUM_CONFIDENCE when absolute MoM spend growth < 25% and CTR volatility < 0.5; otherwise LOW_CONFIDENCE. - Final output per platform-month: - Baselines: current_monthly_spend, current_avg_ctr, current_avg_cpc, current_avg_roas from the monthly aggregates. - Budget recommendation: increase if accelerating and ROAS ≥ 2.0; decrease if decelerating or ROAS < 1.0; otherwise maintain. - Predicted ROAS: +10% when ROAS ≥ 2.5 and CTR momentum improving; −10% when ROAS < 1.5 and CTR momentum declining; otherwise unchanged. - Risk mitigation and strategic recommendation are set to the exact strings defined by the CASE rules. - Revenue scenarios: expected revenue at current ROAS = predicted spend × current avg ROAS; optimized = predicted spend × predicted ROAS; incremental = predicted spend × (predicted ROAS − current avg ROAS). - Success probability: VERY_HIGH when confidence is HIGH and risk is LOW; HIGH when confidence is HIGH/MEDIUM and risk is not HIGH; MEDIUM when confidence is MEDIUM; otherwise LOW. - Metadata: generated timestamp at query run, base date is today, target date is 30 days after the base date. - Filter to months within the last six months; results are ordered by platform ascending and performance month descending.'

business_logic: 'Inputs and key mapping: - Crashes: - Google Play: stg_google_play__stats_crashes_overview (date_day, package_name→app_name, crashes) - Apple Store: stg_apple_store__app_crash_daily (date_day, app_name, crashes) - Installs/Downloads: - Google Play: stg_google_play__stats_installs_overview (date_day, package_name→app_name, device_installs, device_uninstalls) - Apple Store: stg_apple_store__app_store_download_standard_daily (date_day, app_name, total_downloads) - Ratings: - Google Play only: stg_google_play__stats_ratings_overview (date_day, package_name→app_name, average_rating, rolling_total_average_rating), including only rows where average_rating is present (rows with NULL average_rating are excluded). - Platform is set to ''google_play'' or ''apple_store'' per source row. Record assembly (full outer joins; assumes sources are unique per (date_day, app_name, platform)): - Full outer join crashes and installs on (date_day, app_name, platform). - Full outer join ratings using the coalesced (date_day, app_name, platform) from the prior join. - Coalesced keys: date_day = coalesce(crashes.date_day, installs.date_day, ratings.date_day); app_name and platform likewise. Metrics null policy: - crash_count = coalesce(source crashes, 0). - Installs/uninstalls/total_activity: - Google Play: installs = device_installs; uninstalls = device_uninstalls; total_activity = installs + uninstalls. - Apple Store: installs = total_downloads; uninstalls = 0; total_activity = installs. - daily_average_rating and total_average_rating come from Google Play ratings; they are NULL when no rating row exists. Rate calculations (double precision; no rounding): - crash_rate_per_thousand = crashes per 1,000 activities using crash_count and total_activity; if total_activity is 0 or missing, set to 0. - uninstall_rate_percentage = uninstalls as a percent of installs; if installs is 0 or missing, set to 0. Rolling windows and lags (partitioned by app_name and platform; ordered by date_day; row-based using available records only): - 7-row averages: crash_rate_7d_avg = average of crash_rate_per_thousand over up to the last 7 records (including current); uninstall_rate_7d_avg = average of uninstall_rate_percentage over the same; rating_7d_avg = average of daily_average_rating over the same (NULL if all values in the window are NULL). - 30-row metrics: crash_rate_30d_avg = average of crash_rate_per_thousand over up to the last 30 records; installs_30d_sum = sum of installs over up to the last 30 records; crashes_30d_sum = sum of crash_count over up to the last 30 records. - Lags: rating_7d_ago and crash_rate_7d_ago are the values from 7 records earlier. Trends (default to 0 when insufficient history or NULL inputs): - rating_trend_7d = daily_average_rating minus rating_7d_ago when both exist; else 0. - crash_rate_trend_7d = crash_rate_per_thousand minus crash_rate_7d_ago when both exist; else 0. Health score (integer 0–100): - Start at 50. - Rating adjustment using daily_average_rating: +30 (≥4.5), +20 (≥4.0), +10 (≥3.5), +0 (≥3.0), -10 otherwise; if rating is missing it falls to the -10 adjustment. - Crash-rate penalty using crash_rate_7d_avg: 0 (≤1), -5 (≤5), -10 (≤10), -15 (≤20), -20 otherwise. - Uninstall-rate penalty using uninstall_rate_7d_avg: 0 (≤2), -5 (≤5), -10 (≤10), -15 (≤20), -20 otherwise. - Bound the final score to 0–100. Health status (first-match precedence): - Critical if crash_rate_7d_avg > 15. - High Risk if uninstall_rate_7d_avg > 15. - Poor Quality if daily_average_rating < 3.0. - Declining if rating_trend_7d < -0.3. - Unstable if crash_rate_trend_7d > 5. - Excellent if daily_average_rating ≥ 4.0 and crash_rate_7d_avg ≤ 5. - Good if daily_average_rating ≥ 3.5 and crash_rate_7d_avg ≤ 10. - Average otherwise. Volume tier by installs_30d_sum: - High Volume (≥10,000), Medium Volume (≥1,000), Low Volume (≥100), Minimal Volume (<100). Flags (0/1 integers): - needs_immediate_attention = 1 for health_status in (''Critical'',''High Risk''); else 0. - is_high_performing = 1 for health_status=''Excellent''; else 0. - is_declining_quality = 1 if rating_trend_7d < -0.2; else 0. - is_stability_degrading = 1 if crash_rate_trend_7d > 3; else 0. Data quality flag (first-match precedence): - Invalid Health Score if health_score < 0 or > 100. - Invalid Crash Rate if crash_rate_per_thousand < 0. - Invalid Uninstall Rate if uninstall_rate_percentage < 0. - Invalid Rating if daily_average_rating < 0 or > 5. - Valid otherwise. Output filter and timestamp: - Include only rows where date_day, app_name, and platform are not NULL. - analysis_timestamp = current runtime timestamp in the warehouse/session time zone.'
